signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hormuz De-escalation
signals.text: CAD/JPY trades at 112.517 as the JPY continues its dominant G10 outperformance, while CAD lags the complex. The G10 scorecard shows a massive 2.031% spread between the leader (JPY) and laggard (CAD) over the last week. JPY strength is underpinned by a sustained positive Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of +22.9, contrasting with the JPY COT LF net short of -124,575 which suggests significant room for further short-covering. Meanwhile, WTI oil remains under pressure at $75.0 as regional diplomats meet in Amman to discuss de-escalating Strait of Hormuz tensions, stripping away the geopolitical risk premium that typically supports the loonie. The pair remains technically vulnerable after a sustained break below the JPY-based SMA20/50 cluster. Implication: CAD weakness and JPY short-unwinding are the primary G10 drivers, keeping the cross heavy until oil or geopolitical narratives shift. Risk: Hormuz de-escalation talks fail, sparking an oil spike that restores CAD demand.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Fed Rhetoric + Options Skew + Vol Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 157.72, holding below the SMA200 at 158.0 and significantly below the SMA20/50 cluster at 161.25/161.88. Fed Governor Cook's recent warnings that rate hikes remain possible if disinflation stalls provides a hawkish fundamental floor, yet the options market is pricing aggressive downside protection. The 25d Risk Reversal (RR) shows a strong -2.40 put skew, the most extreme in the G10 space, indicating institutional demand for USD/JPY downside hedges despite the 275bp OIS carry advantage for the USD. This creates a volatility divergence: USD/JPY IV at 7.2% is currently sitting 1.1% below its 30-day realized volatility (HV30=8.3%), suggesting the options market is currently underpricing potential breakout risk. Implication: The combination of extreme put skew and negative VRP suggests a market primed for a sharp move if technical resistance at 158.00 holds. Risk: A daily close back above the 158.00 SMA200 level invalidates the bearish momentum.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + RBNZ Hike Bias
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5889 continues to hold above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (range 0.5793–0.5827), reflecting underlying technical strength. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. The NZD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is the strongest in the G10 at +24.4, providing fundamental validation for the RBNZ's hawkishness that specs have yet to price in. Retail sentiment is also heavily skewed, with 76% of traders short, creating a high-conviction setup for a contrarian short-squeeze. Implication: The heavy spec short is fundamentally misaligned with the RBNZ's hiking cycle and positive data surprises, risking a rapid unwind toward 0.6000. Risk: The RBNZ shifts to a neutral stance at the September 2nd meeting, validating the speculative short.

signals.title: AUD/USD — ESI Divergence + Options Vol Premium
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7059, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, but faces building fundamental headwinds. The AUD Economic Surprise Index (ESI) is currently the weakest in the G10 at -15.5, indicating persistent data misses that contradict the current price strength and the +23,616 COT LF net long position. This fundamental decay is reflected in the options market, where AUD/USD IV of 11.2% carries a massive 4.9% premium over realized volatility (HV30=6.3%). This elevated VRP suggests that while the spot price is bid, the market is paying significantly for protection against a reversal. Implication: The data-positioning divergence suggests the AUD rally is overextended, with the high vol premium signaling a lack of institutional conviction in further upside. Risk: RBA delivers a hawkish surprise on August 11, justifying the current positioning and spot levels.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Safe-Haven Flow + Volatility Extreme
signals.text: USD/CHF is trading at 0.8065, testing the SMA50 support level at 0.8039 after failing to hold the SMA20. Despite a massive +375bp OIS carry advantage for the USD, the pair is under pressure as the Swiss Franc gains on disappointing US economic data and safe-haven flows related to Middle East tensions. The USD/CHF volatility landscape is extreme, with IV at 28.5% against an HV30 of only 6.4%, resulting in a massive +22.1% Vol Risk Premium. This suggests that the options market is pricing in a 'tail risk' event far beyond current realized price action, likely reflecting geopolitical intervention or sudden SNB policy shifts. Implication: Carry is being ignored in favor of defensive CHF positioning; the pair remains at the mercy of geopolitical headlines until the vol premium compresses. Risk: A definitive de-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz leads to a rapid carry-trade restoration, targeting 0.8200.
